sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wished arrays had superpowers? The `Arrays` class is here to save the day! It’s like a Swiss Army knife for arrays in Java.

• How to sort, search, and compare arrays effortlessly
• Ways to fill, copy, and convert arrays in one line
• Practical tricks to make your code cleaner and faster

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you’re organizing a bookshelf. You could manually sort each book by title, but wouldn’t it be easier if someone handed you a magic wand to do it instantly? That’s what the `Arrays` class does for your arrays!

The `Arrays` class is a **utility class** in Java’s `java.util` package. It provides static methods to perform common operations on arrays—like sorting, searching, and filling—without writing loops or complex logic.

• **No need to reinvent the wheel**: Why write a sorting algorithm when `Arrays.sort()` exists?
• **Works with all array types**: Primitives (`int[]`, `double[]`) and objects (`String[]`, `Integer[]`).
• **Saves time and reduces bugs**: Less code = fewer mistakes.

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how The Arrays Class works:

steps.title: Before Sorting
steps.description: An unsorted array of numbers looks messy, like a pile of shuffled cards.

steps.title: Apply `Arrays.sort()`
steps.description: The `Arrays.sort()` method rearranges the elements in ascending order—like magic!

steps.title: Search with `Arrays.binarySearch()`
steps.description: Find the position of a value (e.g., `5`) in the sorted array. Returns `-1` if not found.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ `Arrays.sort()`: Sorts arrays in ascending order (primitives or objects).
✓ `Arrays.binarySearch()`: Finds an element in a **sorted** array (faster than linear search).
✓ `Arrays.fill()`: Fills an array with a specific value (e.g., `Arrays.fill(arr, 0)`).
✓ `Arrays.equals()`: Checks if two arrays have the same elements in the same order.
✓ `Arrays.toString()`: Converts an array to a readable string (e.g., `[1, 2, 3]`).

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use `Arrays.toString()` for debugging—no more manual loops!
Always sort before using `binarySearch()` (it won’t work on unsorted arrays).
For large arrays, use `Arrays.parallelSort()` for faster sorting.
donts: Don’t use `==` to compare arrays—it checks references, not content!
Don’t modify arrays while iterating (e.g., sorting during a loop).
sections.protip: Combine `Arrays.copyOf()` with `Arrays.sort()` to create a sorted copy without changing the original array!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is The Arrays Class used in real apps?

examples.how: Sorts product IDs or prices to display results quickly using `Arrays.sort()`.
Fills a game board with default values (e.g., `Arrays.fill(board, ' ')`).
Compares datasets with `Arrays.equals()` to check for duplicates.

problem.description: Write a method that takes an array of integers and returns a **new sorted array** with all duplicates removed. Use the `Arrays` class to simplify your code!
hints: First, sort the array to group duplicates together.
Use a loop to skip duplicates and copy unique elements to a new array.
Try `Arrays.copyOf()` to resize the array at the end.
problem.explanation: 1. Sort the array to group duplicates. 2. Count unique elements by comparing adjacent values. 3. Copy unique elements to a new array. The `Arrays` class handles sorting for you!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 The `Arrays` class is your shortcut for common array operations—no loops needed!
📌 Always sort before searching (`binarySearch` only works on sorted arrays).
📌 Practice with `sort()`, `fill()`, and `equals()` to write cleaner code.
